title: Very happy to finally lay hands on one it is now ...
text:
Very happy to finally lay hands on one it is now sitting in my game room next to my other favorites. I have been watching this item come back in and out of stock for months, and every time I hesitated, it vanished before I could check out. When I saw the restock notification this time, I jumped on it immediately, and I am so glad I did.

I am writing this review after three full plays with a group of four adults, plus one solo run to learn the rules. The components are absolutely gorgeous – the card stock is thick with a linen finish that feels premium, the tokens are chunky, and the artwork on everything is vibrant without being overly busy. The rulebook is clearly laid out, which is a huge relief because I have had to teach many complicated games that required constant rule lookups. This one took about ten minutes to explain, and by the second round everyone was strategizing on their own.

What really sets this game apart is the balance between luck and planning. You can have a perfect strategy, but a few unlucky draws can push you to adapt on the fly, which keeps every session fresh. The replay value seems immense. There are multiple character abilities, variable setup options, and a scoring system that rewards different play styles – aggressive builders, cautious explorers, and even sneaky traders all have viable paths to victory. My last game came down to a single point, and the table erupted into friendly arguments about who should have blocked whom. That is the mark of a great game.

The only minor criticism I have is that the box insert could be a little more efficient; the plastic trays leave some pieces loose if you store it vertically. But that is a small nitpick for such a well-crafted product. For anyone on the fence, do not wait. This one sells out fast for a reason, and I can already tell it will be hitting our table regularly for years to come. If you love medium-weight strategy games with a bit of social interaction, this is a must-buy. Five stars without hesitation.

text:

This Canon looks SLICK; very stylish. The front door automatically opens when it starts printing -- like a kid I will never get over how cool that is. It takes up paper as its printing, so it literally prints a page and then goes right to the next one (vice my HP would take up one page, finish printing a page and spit it out, then take up the next sheet, etc.). It's very quick and the fax and copy functions work with one button.

It's pretty quiet (there's an option for Nighttime printing which I guess makes it even quieter) but shakes the desk when it's moving! Paper cassette holds plenty of paper and the auto feed handler works great for the fax.

The unit is BIG, though. Maybe not bigger than others, but much bigger than my old printer. If you're a work-at-home guy like me, you should measure your area before bying any of these units.

I've already recommended this unit to two friends. I'm very pleased.

title: Opened my EYES!
text:
I am writing this review because I feel compelled to share how profoundly this book shifted my perspective, something I haven't experienced in years of reading. As a professional who thought they had seen it all, I approached this title with a healthy dose of skepticism. I expected generic self-help clichés or superficial advice that we all encounter daily. Instead, what I found was a rigorous, beautifully structured argument that challenges the very foundations of how we perceive reality. The author does not just tell you to open your eyes; they provide the logical framework and the psychological tools necessary to actually do so.

The pacing is excellent. There are no filler chapters designed to pad the word count. Every paragraph serves a specific purpose, building upon the last to create a cohesive narrative that feels both personal and universally applicable. I found myself stopping frequently to reflect on my own biases and assumptions, which was an uncomfortable but necessary process. The writing style is accessible without being condescending, striking a rare balance between academic depth and conversational warmth.

What struck me most was the section on cognitive dissonance and how we rationalize our poor decisions. It was a mirror held up to my own life, revealing patterns I had ignored for decades. This is not a quick fix book. It requires active engagement and honest self-reflection. However, the payoff is immense. Since finishing this book, I have noticed a tangible improvement in my decision-making processes and my ability to empathize with people who hold different viewpoints.

If you are looking for entertainment, this might not be it. But if you are seeking genuine growth and a deeper understanding of the human condition, this book is an absolute necessity. It is rare to find a work that feels so urgently important and timeless all at once. I highly recommend it to anyone willing to do the hard work of seeing the truth.

title: Didn't last longer than a month but customer service saved it
text:
I was really excited when I unboxed these wireless earbuds. The sound quality was crisp, the fit was comfortable, and the battery life actually matched the advertised claims for the first few weeks. I used them daily during my commute and at the gym, and they performed exactly as I had hoped. The pairing was seamless with my phone, and the touch controls were responsive. For about three weeks, I was completely satisfied and even recommended them to a friend.

Then, just shy of the one-month mark, the left earbud stopped holding a charge. It would die after about ten minutes of use, and within a few days it wouldn't power on at all. I tried resetting, cleaning the contacts, and even trying a different charging case didn’t help. I was frustrated because a product that worked so well at first should not fail that quickly. I was ready to leave a scathing review and toss them in the drawer.

But I decided to contact customer service first, and I’m glad I did. The representative responded within hours, asked a few basic troubleshooting questions, and then immediately offered a full replacement—no return shipping fees, no long wait for approval. They shipped a new unit that arrived in three days. The replacement has been working fine for two months now, no issues.

So here’s the thing: the original product clearly had a quality control issue. For the price, I expect more than a month of reliable use. That alone would have been a two stars. However, the customer service experience was genuinely excellent—fast, no hassle, and they stood behind their product. That kind of support is rare these days. So I’m giving four stars: one star deducted for the initial failure, but four because the company made it right and the replacement works as intended. If you buy these, keep the receipt handy, but know that if something goes wrong, they’ll take care of it. I’d probably buy from this brand again because of that service.

text:
As the stars say, I really liked this book. This does not, however, mean it was without its problems.

Issue #1: Stud-in-residence (the police chief) calls ex-stud (contractor/carpenter) "Bob the Builder" - more than once. Both are (understandably) concerned for the MC's safety. When they are trying to talk her into staying safe, they say things like "don't be such a Nancy Drew" or "you're running off like Dora the Explorer".

Seriously? Two adult macho males referring to children's TV programming? I would have let Bob the Builder pass (though it twanged something in my head), but Nancy Drew and Dora the Explorer?

Issue #2: In a small section the author's editor apparently went on break. In the space of just a few pages, I read "peaked into the refrigerator", "share's my blood" and "for Cinnamon and I". All three of these are glaring errors that shouldn't have existed had the writer paid attention through middle school English/Grammar classes.

Having griped about those two issues, I must reiterate that I really liked the book. It had a slight comic book feel to it - A good slice of humor, quirky supporting characters, some adventure and danger, and an ending that I didn't figure out until it was time to do so.

title: Cute
text:
I picked up this "Cute" item after seeing it in a friend’s kitchen, and honestly, it lives up to its name. It’s a small ceramic jar shaped like a little animal face—mine is a cat with a tiny bow. Perfect for holding my loose tea bags, sugar packets, or even as a spare change dish by the door. The craftsmanship is solid: the glaze is smooth, the colors are cheerful, and the lid fits snugly enough to keep out dust. It brings a smile every time I glance at it on my counter.

Functionally, it does what it should. The opening is wide enough to reach in and grab a tea bag without fumbling, and the size is just right for a small countertop. I’ve had it about three months now and the paint hasn’t chipped, even after a gentle drop onto the tile floor (don’t ask). The interior is glazed too, so it’s easy to wipe clean if you use it for sugar or salt.

Why only four stars? Two minor issues. First, the packaging was a bit skimpy—just tissue paper and a thin bubble wrap envelope. The jar arrived fine, but for a ceramic item, I’d expect more padding. Second, the base is a little uneven. It wobbles slightly on a perfectly flat surface. Not enough to tip over, but noticeable if you’re fussy about things sitting level. For the price (around $12), it’s a charming little accent piece, but it’s not a precision product.

Overall, if you want a whimsical touch for your kitchen or desk and don’t mind a slight wobble, this “Cute” jar is a solid choice. It’s better than a lot of the mass-produced kitsch out there. I’d buy another as a gift, though I’d re-pack it more carefully. Recommended for anyone who enjoys a little personality in their home décor.

It is rare to find something in the Toys and Games category that feels like it was built to last rather than just being made of cheap, disposable plastic.

Whether you are looking for a birthday gift or just something to keep the house quiet for a while, this is a great choice. It does exactly what it claims to do without any unnecessary bells and whistles that usually just break. It is simple, effective, and provides great value for the money. I have already recommended it to a few other parents in my neighborhood because it is one of the few purchases that actually lived up to the description. If you are on the fence about getting this, just go for it. It is a reliable product that serves its purpose perfectly. It is refreshing to buy something that works exactly as advertised without any hidden catches or assembly headaches. The worst part is that my dog didn't even go after it that hard. It's not like she was shredding it daily. Just normal use and it fell apart. Overall, a letdown. If your pet is extremely gentle and barely touches their things, maybe this works. But if you have an average, playful dog, look elsewhere. It looks great in the photos, but real-world use is disappointing. I can't recommend spending your money on this.

title: Excellent account of the "Emergency"
text:
I served in the army in Malaya in 1957-58, and found this book to be an excellent "refresher course" when writing my own stories for my family; we have long-standing connections with Malaya, from before WWII until just after Merdeka, and I was able to fill in some gaps and correct some errors.

I've deducted one star because of two problems: first, it is in serious need of an index, and second, there isn't much coverage of the later stages just before Merdeka (August 1957) - perhaps the CTs were effectively beaten by then, but we felt (perhaps mistakenly) that Malaya was still definitely a war zone. I suppose that when you are in the jungle and your rations are being parachuted in you get a distorted view of history!

This book dates from 1971, so naturally does not have some of the information that later writers have been able to find as records are released. I recommend Margaret Shennan's biography of John Davis, "Our Man in Malaya" (2007), as an excellent addition to the field. But of course F. Spencer Chapman's classic, "The Jungle is Neutral", is required reading for anyone trying to understand what jungle warfare really feels like.

title: Exceeded My Expectations In Every Way!
text:
Reign of Shadows exceeded my expectations in every way and kept me on my toes the entire story. Danger around every corner, romance, and adventure had me loving every second of Reign of Shadows. I was seriously hooked until the last sentence, and I defiantly did not want it to end there. Luna is an exceptional heroine in this novel, even with her disadvantages she is stronger and tougher than most of the other survivors left in her world. I could not help but want to root for her in every way.

There is a bit of romance, and I love that it does not come out forced as sometimes I find other book will do just to have a romance aspect to the story. It has a natural feeling to it, and it even acts like a beacon of hope in a world of eternal darkness. With switching points-of-view, readers get to experience the story from both Luna’s perspective and Fowler’s perspective. I have always been a fan of the multiple viewpoint stories, as I think it provides a 360 view of the story and the characters. I think it is a needed feature in Reign of Shadows as these two characters both have many thoughts and secrets that only readers get to experience through the changing perspective.

The setting and world building of Reign of Shadows is perfect. It is a dark and creepy world where dark dwellers rise up from the ground every day to eat anything living and without any real sunlight, survivors of the eclipse on get one hour of peace when the dark is just bright enough to drive the dwellers back underground. The description of the dwellers were detailed enough to nearly give me nightmares after reading Reign of Shadows.

This is the first book of Sophie Jordan’s that I have had the chance to read, but I have always heard amazing things about her other books. Now I know that I have definitely been missing out, and I am setting to rectify that mistake as soon as possible. Her writing sucks you deep in the story and holds you there until the very end brings you back to reality. Only the truly best stories can offer that type of hold over a reader.

My only very minor gripe is that the control panel buttons are a bit basic, and the buttons feel a bit plasticky. But for the price I paid, I consider that a negligible trade-off. title: Felt like a boss shutting down sector 12
text:
Had your emotional subroutines removed? Got an unproductive sector? Fret no more! Shockwave is here to shut them down and toss those unproductive Decepticons over to Project Nemesis where they're needed. He's small enough to fit in your pocket so you can stroll around Cybertron with him to keep those other sectors in line. War for Cybertron reference aside....

PARENTS: This is an awesome little toy for young and adult Transformers fans. Shockwave is this character's name and he is one of the primary villains (Decepticon team) in the Transformer shows. He's basically 2nd in command to Megatron (the chief villain/antagonist). This Shockwave model is only 13 steps to transform, which may prove difficult for young children who are inexperienced with Transformer toys. For those children, I'd recommend the 1-step line of toys (Cybertron Adventures and Rescue Bots). My 4 year old has a lot of exposure to my complex Transformer collection, so he powers through 13 steps without a sweat. Note that the hand cannon is detachable, so be wary of losing this to the couch cushion abyss like the rest of your kid's toy accessories. Lastly, this is a "core class" figure, so it's relatively small at 3.5" when standing in robot mode.

My opinion of this model is very positive. For such a small scale, the sculpting work is super detailed and it does a near perfect job of capturing Shockwave's "Gen1" appearance (except for the angry brow). His robot-mode transformation is engineered well, tight joints/pivots and no fear of breaking any brittle pieces. The alt-mode (a tank?) is acceptable, but I've no major complaints about either mode.

title: Best new table-top or Skype-it role playing game!
text:
I have played this game both as a play tester Storyteller and Player for many years now, and I love it. Everyone (especially the stalwart Dungeons & Dragons players disappointed with the watered down D&D latest editions) loves the game system and basic premise: to become emperor at all costs (even at the expense of the other players). In that respect, it's like Celebrity Apprentice or Survivor in that the players work together but all are really scheming to outdo each other to eventually rise to such power as to become Emperor or Empress.

The whole game has an open spell system (this book [[ASIN:0692088644 The Adventurer's Rulebook: An Essential Component of the Immortal Empires Role-Playing Game for Mature Players]] ) where you create your own spells with a straightforward point system, 10 huge magical fighting arts (this book and the Storyteller's Codex) with 40 fighting art powers each, nonmagical Talents for fighters and thieves, politicians and assassins, and much more.

The system uses d10s only, and the opposed roll system is perfect. It allows the weaker characters a chance against the great characters, as in real life. Overall, it's a great game, in my humble opinion, and a great learning tool for math, vocabulary, and yes, even Latin!

To get a feel for the game, because it is costly (but it is well worth it as these are premium 8.5x11" full color laminate hard cover books), people should order the three available novels:

[[ASIN:1543132170 Mirror Motives: Immortal Empires of the Seventh Age (Immortal Empires Sextology) (Volume 1)]]

Our cats get very verbal in the wee hours clamoring for us to feed them, so we decided to let them worship a machine instead. After seeing more food was to be had, he stuck his paw right up and was rewarded. We tried putting cardboard over the mouth of the bowl to make it too far for him to reach, but he could still bump it, even when drinking out of his separate water dish! Sitting at home, the feeder would also, completely at random, dispense food, which would of course get the cats all excited. The smarter cat was not only getting rewards for bumping (or hopping on to) the feeders (yes, both), he was getting random snacks. The plastic spindles that meter the food are weak and ineffective. Written by Kelly Long, "A Marriage of the Heart" tells the story of Rachel Yoder, an Amish girl who has been raised by her strict father after her mother's death. Long tells Yoder's story of falling in love with her husband and facing her demons. "What the Heart Sees" by Kathleen Fuller tells the story of Ellie Chupp, a young Amish woman who lost her sight as well as her best friend in a horrible accident. When her best friend's former fiance shows up, Ellie's attempts to deal with her disability are disrupted. However, love is just around the corner for Ellie. "Healing Hearts" by Beth Wiseman tells the story of Naaman and Levina Lapp. After 30 years of marriage, they are facing an empty nest, which is something that Naaman especially cannot deal with. He leaves for year, but when he returns he finds that things are not as he hoped they would be. Levina is cold and confused, dealing with whether or not she can trust the man who left her.

I found these three novellas to be enjoyable. Easy to read and interesting, they offer insight to the lives of the Amish, as well as insight into the lives of people in general. The stories are heartwarming and touching, and I would definitely recommend the book.

title: The kind of book that you'll be reluctant to finish.
text:
Ever since the quality of Elizabeth George's books took a nosedive, I've been searching for another favorite mystery author. I've found her. And interestingly, like Ms. George, Deborah Crombie is an American woman who sets her mysteries in England.

The book has three threads: one is the ongoing romantic relationship between Superintendent Kincaid and his partner, Gemma James. A second is the mystery itself, involving a beautiful woman whose body is found carefully laid out in a park. The third is the genesis of the relationship among some of the characters/suspects and their families, a relationship which began back when English children were transported to the countryside to spare them the horrors of the World War II Blitz.

All three themes are handled beautifully. The characters of Duncan Kincaid and Gemma James continue to develop believably throughout this series. (This is, I believe, the sixth Kincaid/James book). The real-life problems and uncertainties they encounter while trying to maintain their family and professional obligations, and leave time for themselves and each other, will strike a believable chord with anyone old enough to have gone through this phase of life. The mystery is complex and unpredictable enough to be challenging but not confusing. The ending is beautiful - it settles both the mystery and the unresolved pain from the events of the 1940's.

If you haven't discovered the Crombie/Kincaid/James series yet, I recommend starting with the first one, "A Share in Death," which was nominated for an Agatha as best first novel of 1993. But I've read all of the first six, and they're all excellent.

title: A Must-Have
text:
The authors offer truly groundbreaking insights and methods in this book, and I will cite a few, but the depth and breadth of their work is far too vast to encapsulate here. They note the plethora of unhelpful, anecdotal advice that often passes for wisdom in similar books, and instead provide scientifically documented, step-by-step methods for defining and achieving goals. They provide compelling examples of how these techniques have been implemented. The most fascinating story, in my opinion, involved the eradication of the guinea worm, an endemic parasite that can grow up to three feet long and emerges through the skin causing tremendous pain. The authors cited techniques employed by Carter Foundation workers to teach villagers how to filter their water and prevent reinfestation of water sources by infected persons. Carter Foundation workers sought positive deviants (villages who had learned their own ways of avoiding guinea worm infestation) to teach other villages what to do.

I noted many techniques that I myself had discovered by trial and error, such as perfect practice, which involves working on improving specific elements of a task; they cite basketball freethrowing, where perfect practice includes improving followthrough, elbow position, etc., as opposed to results oriented practice that can reinforce poor technique, e.g. shoot until I get 20 baskets. As a Chemistry teacher, I inherently implemented many of these techniques. This book provided me with more insight and concrete guidance than most of the teaching and education books I was provided in my teacher training.

This is one of the most enlightening books I have ever read on human behavior. Having borrowed this book from the library, I now plan to purchase it (the actual ink and paper version), because I know I will refer to it again and again.

title: Finally, a wired adapter that works with my Insignia Roku TV
text:
Have a Roku TV that is supposed to be wireless-only (why can't they include an rj45 jack anyway?). Even with a wireless router positioned right behind it, still had problems with adaptive streaming sites changing resolution streams multiple times during playback. Searched Roku forums and found an older Belkin adapter mentioned, but that's not available, and has a replacement listed that did not work for me. My son had purchased an HDE adapter for his Wii some time ago (and neglected to tell me), so I tried that and it did work with my TV. so I got one of those, too. Don't know if it was just defective, but the new one didn't work, neither on my TV or the Wii, or even on a laptop, so back it went. Still searching, because I proved to myself that something could work. Finally found this brand mentioned as working after another search, even though the seller says it doesn't. At this point, for $12 I figured what the heck. And it worked... With the other adapters not working I had tried everything, resetting to original settings, unplugging and re-plugging power, USB slot, Cat 6 cable, nothing.

With this adapter, all I had to do was unplug the power cord after installing, plug it back in, turn it on, and it worked. A little slower initial boot, but that's pretty minor to have a working wired connection with no more adaptive streaming fluctuations. Before, Netflix thought i only had 4 Mbps down on a good day, and afterward, that had tripled (according to the test in their app). With another separate speed test app, I'm actually getting as high as 54 Mbps down (out of 60 possible) now.

Edit, 6 weeks later, still using it every day, still working fine except for one incident where it didn't connect after a power on, but I just removed power again and restarted, and has been OK since.

title: Works with Eufy G30 Verge
text: This is the same tape that is included with the Eufy G30 Verge. We purchased a total of 4 rolls of this product to mark off areas in our home. It works when it is exposed on the floor and also when it is under the very edge of thin carpets. We adhered to both the floor and carpet edge, and have not had any issues with lifting. Two important things we have learned: first, all this device needs to sneak through a spot is 4 to 6 inches of gap in the tape. When planning this layout, and you should plan it before you cut it, make sure you are not leaving any gaps in the tape. Secondly, if you are concerned about damaging your floor with the 3M double-sided tape that is enclosed, we used 3M command strips with a 3-pound weight classification. We were able to purchase a package of these separate of command hooks they are typically used with. Since we have hardwood floors, we thought this was a worthy investment. All tape was mounted with the light side facing upward. The device has not crossed any of the magnetic barriers including thresholds. I should add that we do not have any metal threshold in our home, it is all wood, tile, carpet, and vinyl. The tape is an investment that can be costly but it is absolutely worth it. We returned a similar product because it did not work but this barrier tape has performed 100%. It also has a lower profile then other barrier tape we tried so it lays nice and flat under area rugs and in high traffic areas. Highly recommend.

title: Tiny charger with very detailed information in the product description
text: This product came with the single battery charger and 19" USB-A to micro-USB cable.  There's no manual included but all the information is on the product listing and description.  For about $6, this good deal if you wanted a compact single cell charger.  It's rated at 1A charging.  So, it's a fast charger compared to the normally 300 mA or 500 mA chargers.  The 18650 battery I'm charging does get warm when charging but that's normal for fast chargers.  Though it could mean it would not help extend the life of the battery.  Please note that this charger was designed only for Li-ON batteries of a certain size.  Don't try charging Ni-MH, Ni-Cd, AA, AAA, AAAA, nor C batteries.  They are normally 1.2 V batteries and will more than likely get damaged by charging at 4.2v 1A.  It's a compact design built for portability.  I don't see the sense in complaining about the micro-USB end of the cable because it goes right into the charger base.  And the USB-A end would fit in any USB 2.0 or USB 3.0 port or wall adapter.  The item works right out of the box.

UPDATE 08/12/2018 REPLACED BELT

After about a year of daily use I noticed a black powder accumulating on the ground under the belt cover. I figured out it was the belt wearing out. I purchased a new one (OEM PN 5PK1320). I couldn't find any instructions on the Sunny site but it's not that hard. Remove all the screws from the belt cover, including the one that holds it in place on the left side of the bike. You might have to remove the right pedal to get the cover completely off. Once you have the cover off, remove the 10-mm retaining nuts on the two eyebolts that align the flywheel, then loosen the two 19-mm nuts that hold the flywheel in place. Lift the flywheel far enough up to slip the old belt out and the new belt in. Align the belt on the front pulley and reattach the 10-mm eyebolts to the frame, then tighten the 19-mm flywheel bolts. Place the belt on the back pulley as far as you can get it, then turn the crank to get it on the rest of the way, the same way you get a chain back onto a bicycle chain ring. Put the cover back on and you are done.

text:
Story: I liked this story much more than the first book of the series (Need). I found that this plot line is better developed and more captivating. I wanted to keep reading and to know what was going to happen. And the end of the novel made me itch to read the third of the series. One BIG surprise in particular really took me off guard. Ahhh! If you read this book, you will know what I'm talking about!

Characters: All the main characters are the same, likeable characters. Zara develops quite nicely in this book. And there is a new character, Astley, who I think I like. Astley is the new king pixie in town, but he claims to be different - he claims to be good. I like the way he is presented (just hope we can trust him!).

Writing: The writing quality is better in this book. It is still a bit weak, but it was able to captivate my interest. There are a few errors (or typos), but nothing really worth mentioning. I only mention the errors because there were soooo many in the first book. Big improvement here!

Uniqueness/Creativity: This book was also much better in the uniqueness and creativity department. Jones came up with unique and creative elements that I've never heard of before. So, yay! Good for her! And I didn't feel like I was reading Twilight this time!!

Overall: Overall, this book was good. It kept my interest so that I wanted to keep reading. I am itching to read the third book of the series! Can't wait to see what happens! Would I recommend this book? I would recommend it to anyone who really liked Twilight by Stephanie Meyer. If you are bothered by weak quality of writing, then I would suggest staying away. It's a good story, but the quality is a bit weak. Side note: I totally like how the king pixies need a queen in order to be strong(er) - I think it's awesome that women are needed by the men in this way! Hehe :)

text:
I have been searching for a reliable solution for my golden retriever, Buster, for quite some time now, and I must admit, I approached this purchase with a mix of high hopes and significant skepticism. My dog has always been prone to chewing on things he shouldn't, particularly during his teething phase and when he is left alone for extended periods. The product description promised durability, mental stimulation, and hours of engaging playtime, which sounded too good to be true. After using it for about three weeks, I feel compelled to share my honest experience to help other pet owners make an informed decision.

First, let’s address the build quality. On one hand, the material feels sturdy and the design is intuitive enough for a dog to understand quickly. Buster picked it up in less than five minutes, which was impressive. He spends a good amount of time trying to get the treats out, and that alone has kept him occupied while I work from home. The Kong-like shape is effective for freezing treats, which adds an extra layer of engagement during hot summer days. From a utility standpoint, it does exactly what it claims to do regarding keeping a pet busy and distracted from household furniture.

However, there are notable downsides that prevent this product from earning a five-star rating in my book. The main issue is the cleanup process, which is unnecessarily complicated. It has many small crevices and seams where food particles get trapped. No matter how much I scrub it with hot soapy water, I still worry about bacteria buildup or that strange smell that sometimes lingers after washing. This is a significant drawback for a product that is supposed to be a daily staple in your home. Additionally, while Buster loves it, he has managed to crack a small section after a particularly aggressive play session, despite the claims of being "indestructible." It hasn’t broken apart completely, but it has raised concerns about its long-term durability for powerful chewers.

For light to moderate chewers who are willing to put in the extra effort to clean it thoroughly, this might be a decent option. It offers good value for the price point and provides the mental enrichment that dogs need. However, if you have a heavy-duty destroyer like mine, or if you simply do not have the time to meticulously clean complex toys, you might want to look elsewhere. It is a decent product overall, but it lacks the polish and robustness that would make it a true household essential. I would recommend it with caveats, not as a blanket endorsement for every dog owner.

title: Best of the pre-PEP or pre-W series works
text:
Perhaps because of a lack of publication or perhaps because of a general lack of distribution of his ideas (Peirce tended to write only for other philosophers and logicians), Peirce's philosophical thinking was not well known until Eisele's "New Elements of Mathematics" (NEM), and the Peirce Edition Project's W series: "The Chronological Writings of Charles Sanders Peirce". Buchler's work is easily the best introduction to the work of Peirce prior to the availability of NEM and the W series.

Buchler worked from an earlier collection of Peirce's writings, called the CP series, consisting of 8 volumes of poorly edited papers presented in such a way as to not show the depth, or originality of his thought, or the evolutionary growth in the depth and power of his thought.

Nevertheless, Buchler's volume is still an excellent, easy to read, and easy to understand (relative to Peirce's depth of thinking) introduction to the immensity of the thought of Charles Peirce. I recommend it as a great reading value.

What I did not expect was that it would survive a full cycle in my washing machine wash – including the spin dry – without any warping, fading, or peeling of the edges. I know that sounds crazy, but here is the story.

I was moving my office to a new room and, in the chaos, my mat ended up in a pile of the laundry pile. My spouse grabbed it thinking it was a load of towels without checking. When I found it later, my heart sank. To my absolute shock, it came out looking brand new. No curling, no frayed stitching, no color bleed. The rubber base stayed perfectly flat, and the fabric top wasn’t pilled or fuzzy. That incident turned me into a believer.

Now I actually wash it on purpose every month. The dirt, coffee drips, and pen marks that used to haunt me are gone with a simple cold wash and low-heat dry. It comes out of the dryer smelling fresh and lies flat on my desk within minutes. The non-slip backing still grips my desk like the first day I unrolled it. The size is generous – fits my keyboard mouse, plus a notebook, with room to spare. The only minor note is that if you overload your washing machine with heavy items, the mat might get folded over during the cycle; I just place it alone on delicate, and it works perfectly.

For anyone who eats at their desk, has kids, or just hates the thought of buying a new mat every six months – this thing is a lifesaver. It’s sturdy, professional-looking, and unkillable. Five stars, no hesitation.

title: Beautiful Photos - Good Healthy Recipes
text:
Mediterranean food has a reputation for being not only delicious, but healthy. The diet is rich in fruits and vegetables as well as healthy oils and lean meats and fish. There are dozens, maybe hundreds of good Mediterranean cookbooks out there, and one that is excellent and includes a huge number of recipes for variety is 1000 Mediterranean Meals: Every Recipe You Need for the Healthiest Way to Eat by Valentina Harris. This cookbook has everything: appetizers, side dishes, soups, salads, mains with or without meat and even desserts. Although they are touted as healthier dishes, they are still mouthwatering, and no one will suspect that eating them will contribute to better health.

Almost all of the recipes include a photograph, which makes the book appealing. Most cooks want to know what the dish should look like. The recipes are written in the classic style with a list of ingredients and easy-to-follow instructions that cooks at all levels can successfully make them.

The variety of the dishes is vast, and there is something for every taste. Most of the recipes include several variations to that everyone can individualize them to their personal tastes. The recipes come from several of the twenty-one countries that border the Mediterranean Sea. Popular classics are included, such as Hummus and Tzatziki, as well as some unique dishes like Huevos Revueltos and Egyptian Sweet Couscous.

Anyone who likes Mediterranean food will love reading and cooking from this excellent cookbook. There will be dozens of recipes that appeal to almost every cook.

Special thanks to NetGalley for supplying a review copy of this book.

title: A fantastic thriller!
text:
THE VACATION by T.M. Logan primarily follows Kate, a wife and mother of two meeting up with her three best friends and their families at a stunning vineyard villa in France for a vacation to celebrate their 40th birthdays. It is meant to be a time to reconnect with each other and their families with good wine, good food and good company. Things aren’t starting off on an ideal note, however.

Kate has a feeling that something is going on with her husband and she manages to log into his phone to check his messages. She sees a back and forth conversation which seems to confirm that her husband is having an affair. Worst yet, the messages imply that the other woman is one of her best friends. As Kate seeks to identify the traitorous friend, it is clear that all of her friends have secrets to hide.

I have been in the mood for thrillers and this one did not disappoint. Once I got into the story, I could not put it down! We are primarily reading from Kate’s POV, hearing her suspicions, seeing her interactions with her friends and family. The author also gives us occasional chapters from the perspective of other characters, Kate’s friends, their husbands and the kids as well. It seems that almost everyone has something to hide and the author does a great job of dropping clues to redirect Kate’s suspicions and the readers’ as well.

This is very much a slow burn book for the first three-quarters or so. There is a lot of family drama and mystery going on which creates that slow build up to the last quarter where things really start to happen, ramping up the thriller elements. On top of the issues of what is going on with Kate’s wife, there are clearly secrets between the teens of their families and with the other women. The slow burn is done very well and it kept me entirely hooked throughout as the author takes the time to really delve into the different characters and potential suspects for everything that is going on.

I would highly recommend adding THE VACATION by T.M. Logan to your TBR!
